reading.body:
Ten frontier technology risks are being modelled before pricing: systemic alignment loss, post-quantum gaps, autonomous fleet liability, brain computer interface software, decentralised compute, neuromorphic and optical hardware, AI-assisted synthetic biology, digital twin drift, synthetic media manipulation, AI-designed compound errors.

The common thread is absence of established failure statistics. Neuromorphic and optical hardware explicitly lacks them, and the other categories involve systems too new for actuarial history. Modelling therefore precedes pricing, which means these risks are being assessed for insurability rather than quoted.

Several entries connect directly to AI infrastructure. Decentralised compute networks raise hardware security questions that cannot be centrally assured, autonomous fleet liability shifts risk to cloud infrastructure, and digital twin synchronisation drift creates claims when simulations diverge from physical plants. These are compute and software risks, not energy or grid risks.

The ten categories do not include power supply, grid constraints, or building capacity. They also give no premium, limit, or loss figures, so they show a modelling agenda rather than a priced market. Readers should not infer that any of these risks are currently insured.
